sources.citation: StressTyp2 database SQL dump (StressTyp2-v1-archive-0415, 2015) held by the project
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ngaing occurs only in the ISO-639-3 code table ('nnf','PG','L','Ngaing'); no StressTyp2 entry.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. doi:10.15144/PL-A23.45
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2 on Ngaing gives only location, 800-900 speakers, dialect chain with Neko/Nekgini. Sec. 6.1 (pp. 66-67) phonology remarks are stock-level: 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat. In none of these languages does it carry a heavy functional load.' Nothing specific to Ngaing.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1965. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific Fascicle Five. Anthropological Linguistics 7(9). (ERIC ED010365)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 54: 'Maipang (Ngaing), with more than 850 speakers' in a bare list of Rai Coast languages after Capell 1962; nothing structural.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG, Languages of Papua New Guinea: 'Language: Ngaing [nnf]' page, https://pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/languages/language/nnf
sources.note: Page only links to the archive search for nnf; the search pages and the sil.org file server return an automated-access block (not reachable by automated download) by automated download, so SIL-PNG holdings (possible OPD) could not be enumerated.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2017. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (OAPEN open access, archive.org oapen-20.500.12657-23719)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 45 documentation listing: 'Ngaing [nnf] 2,020; comparative studies: Claassen and McElhanon 1970, Ross 1995' - i.e. no phonology, sketch or grammar known to the authors; the chapter's prosody section (3.x 'tonal and accent systems') does not mention Ngaing.
Only source is the McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 wordlist; no prosodic information.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page ngai1241 and Glottolog 5.1 CLDF values (med = 4 'a wordlist or less', best ref Mura 1998 word list book)
sources.note: Nothing; confirms most extensive description is a wordlist. Reference records 548072 (Claassen 1968 wordlist 12pp), 569336/547631 (Boswell 1988 Ngaing and Mari wordlists), 50871 (Mura 1998), 547758 (Gray et al. 2015 survey with a Sibog = Ngaing wordlist) inspected as JSON.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1975. North-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 527-567. Pacific Linguistics C-38. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.527

sources.note: Ngaing appears only in the language list and map (Gusap-Mot Family, b.); no stress/accent/tone statement anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent full text layer).

sources.citation: Joshua Project language page nnf; en.wikipedia 'Ngaing language'; de.wikipedia 'Ngaing' (ethnographic refs: Lawrence 1965, Kempf 1992/1996/2003)
sources.note: Nothing linguistic; Joshua Project reports Bible portions 2004-2010 (no NT), so the earlier scan's 'SIL did NT translation in Ngaing' is not confirmed. Archive.org full-text search of 'Ngaing' with stress/accent/syllable/phonology/orthography/pronunciation returned only anthropological and bibliographic hits.
